changes.text: 居里夫妇把制备镭的方法毫无保留地公开，镭工业因此自由发展；他们自己却长期缺钱、缺场地。到1921年，她的实验室仍设备不足，靠美国妇女募捐，居里夫人才得到一克镭。这是一笔两边都有分量的账。

The Curies published their method for preparing radium without reserve, and the radium industry grew freely on it. They themselves long went without money and without a proper workplace. In 1921 her laboratory still lacked sufficient equipment, and a subscription raised by American women finally put a gram in Marie Curie's hands. It is a ledger with weight on both sides.
1921年5月20日，白宫。美国妇女把一克镭赠给它的发现者，可镭本身并不在现场。哈定总统交给居里夫人的是一把小金钥匙，用来打开运送镭的箱子。装镭的管子还在“局”里，那里的官员主动提出代为测量、装箱并送上船。

May 20, 1921, the White House. The women of America gave a gram of radium to its discoverer, but the radium itself was not in the room. What President Harding placed in Mme. Curie's hands was a small golden key, the one that opened the casket devised for transporting the radium. The tubes of radium were still at the Bureau, whose officials had kindly offered to make the measurements and to take care of the packing and delivery to the ship.
一克镭的市价是十万美元。而制备镭的方法，是她和皮埃尔·居里多年前毫无保留地公开的，镭工业正靠它发展起来、高价卖货。公开了方法的她，实验室里那点镭当时只用于为医院提取射气，要靠募捐才能把研究继续下去。这笔账，她在书里一项一项算过。

A gram of radium then sold for one hundred thousand dollars. The process for preparing it had been published years earlier, without reserve, by Marie Curie and Pierre Curie, and the radium industry was now thriving on that very process and selling its product at a high price. She had helped give the method away, yet the radium in her laboratory was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use, and it took a subscription to enable her to go on with her work. In her book she worked through that account line by line.
事情要从1890年代末的巴黎说起。居里夫妇想把一种新放射性物质提纯到能确认是新元素，可他们没有地方干活、没有人手，也没有钱。沥青铀矿很贵，他们买不起足够的量。当时这种矿物的主要来源在波希米亚的圣约阿希姆斯塔尔，奥地利政府在那里经营一座提铀的矿。矿上的残渣还从没用过，他们相信镭和一部分钋就在残渣里。靠维也纳科学院的影响，他们以优惠价拿到几吨残渣。起初的费用出自自己的积蓄，后来才得到少量补助。

The story begins in Paris in the late 1890s. The Curies wanted to purify a new radioactive substance far enough to be sure it was a new element, and they had nowhere to work, no one to help, and no money. Pitchblende was an expensive mineral, and they could not afford to buy a sufficient quantity. At that time the principal source of this mineral was at St. Joachimsthal in Bohemia, where the Austrian government worked a mine for the extraction of uranium. Its residues had so far not been used at all, and they believed the radium, and part of the polonium, would be found in them. Through the influence of the Vienna Academy of Sciences they secured several tons of the residues at an advantageous price. In the beginning the costs came out of their own pockets; only later were they given a few subventions and some help from outside sources.
这两年他们几乎无人相助。这里要补一句：实验室杂工珀蒂常在能挤出的时间里搭手；1898年，学校的实验室主任之一贝蒙临时帮过忙；1900年前后，青年化学家德比埃尔纳加入。分工后皮埃尔研究镭的性质，她负责把镭提纯成纯盐。她一次处理多达二十公斤材料，棚里堆满沉淀物和液体；她要搬运容器、转移液体，再用铁棒连续几小时搅拌铸铁锅里沸腾的物料。

For two years they worked there practically unaided. One qualification: the laboratory helper, Petit, kept lending a hand in whatever time he could spare; G. Bemont, one of the laboratory chiefs at the School, gave temporary help in 1898; and around 1900 the young chemist André Debierne joined them. Once the work was divided, Pierre studied the properties of radium while Marie pushed ahead with the chemical experiments aimed at preparing pure radium salts. She worked with as much as twenty kilogrammes of material at a time, until the hangar was full of great vessels of precipitates and liquids: moving the containers about, transferring the liquids, and stirring the boiling material in the cast-iron basin with an iron bar, for hours at a stretch.
这时日内瓦方面来请皮埃尔：那里物质条件更好，还能过上近似乡居的宁静生活。按居里夫人的记述，这个决定很艰难，皮埃尔动了心。最后让他定下来不去的，是他们正对镭做的研究，他怕这样的变动打断它。此时，索邦为医科学生而设的P.C.N.物理教席正好空缺。他申请后，在庞加莱影响下获聘；她则受托在塞夫尔的女子师范学校讲物理课。他们留在巴黎，收入增加了，工作却更难：P.C.N.学生众多，双重教学让皮埃尔非常疲惫。

Then Geneva came calling for Pierre, offering material advantages and the opportunity of a life comparable in its tranquillity with that in the country. In Marie Curie's account the decision was a grave one, and Pierre was tempted. What finally settled it was the radium research itself, since he feared the interruption that such a change must involve. At this moment the chair of physics in the Sorbonne's P.C.N. course was vacant; this was the physics, chemistry and natural history curriculum compulsory for medical students. He applied, and was appointed through the influence of Henri Poincaré, who was anxious to free him from the necessity of quitting France. Marie was given charge of the physics lectures at the Normal School for Girls at Sèvres. They stayed in Paris and their income increased, but working conditions grew harder: the P.C.N. had very large numbers of students, and Pierre's double teaching load fatigued him greatly.

还有一件事，她在书里两处都写到。按她的叙述，在她同意之下，皮埃尔·居里拒绝从发现中获取任何物质利益，英译此处作「took no copyright」。他们把研究结果和制备镭的确切方法毫无保留地发表，来问的人也都得到答复。自传笔记里她又说了一遍：夫妇二人一贯不从发现中获取物质利益，方法从一开始就全部公开，没有申请专利，也不在工业开发中保留任何好处，此处英译作「took out no patent」。书里没写这个决定的日期。

There is something else she writes about in two places in the book. In Marie Curie's telling, and with her agreement, Pierre Curie refused to draw any material profit from the discovery. As the English translation of the biography puts it, "We took no copyright": they published without reserve all the results of their research as well as the exact processes of the preparation of radium, and gave whatever information was asked of them. In the autobiographical notes she says it again: the two of them always refused to draw any material profit from the discovery, the process was published from the beginning, and they took out no patent and reserved no advantage in any industrial exploitation. The book gives no date for the decision.
钱还是不够。受这次试验启发，法国实业家阿尔梅·德·利尔办起一座真正的镭工厂，把产品卖给医生；医生们对镭的生物效应和可能的疗法已有兴趣。项目成功了，因为他能雇到居里夫妇训练过的人。镭从此有了稳定货源，价格很高：制备条件特殊，制镭所需矿物的价格又立刻上涨。德·利尔出于好意，在厂里给他们一小块工作地方和一部分费用。其余的钱有的是他们自己的，有的来自补助，最大的一笔是1902年科学院给的两万法郎。

The money was still short. Inspired by their attempt, a French industrialist, Armet de Lisle, took what seemed at that epoch the daring step of founding a veritable radium factory to furnish the product to physicians, whose interest in the biological effects of radium and its possible therapeutic applications had been aroused by the publication of various investigations. The project proved a success because he could employ men already trained by the Curies in the delicate processes of the manufacture. Radium was now regularly placed on sale, at a high price it is true, given the special conditions under which it had to be made and the immediate rise in the cost of the minerals necessary to its production. Armet de Lisle, in an entirely disinterested manner, placed a little working place in his factory at their disposition, together with a part of the means necessary to use it. Other funds were added either by the Curies themselves or through subventions, the most important of which, accorded by the Academy of Sciences in 1902, amounted to 20,000 francs.
多年后，她在自传笔记里把账摊开。镭在矿石里含量极小，价格很高；镭又能治好多种疾病，所以制造利润很大。他们放弃的，是一笔本可留给子女的财富。更值得考虑的是许多朋友的反对：若当初保住权利，本可筹钱建一所像样的镭研究所，不必经历那些一直拖累两人、至今仍拖累她的难处。她承认朋友们的看法并非没有道理（英译作「not without reason」），但仍然认为他们做得对。

Years later, in the autobiographical notes, she laid out the rest of the ledger. Radium is found in minerals in very small quantities, so its price is very high, and the profits of its manufacture have been great, since the substance is used to cure a number of diseases. What they sacrificed in renouncing the exploitation of their discovery, then, was a fortune, one that could after them have gone to their children. And what was even more to be considered, she wrote, was the objection of many of their friends, who argued "not without reason" that if they had guaranteed their rights they could have had the financial means of founding a satisfactory Institute of Radium, without the difficulties that had been such a handicap to both of them and were still a handicap to her. She conceded the point and held her ground all the same: "Yet, I still believe that we have done right."

梅洛尼为本书写了引言，后来在纽约发起募捐。她见到居里夫人时，居里夫人说美国约有五十克镭，巴尔的摩四克、丹佛六克、纽约七克；在法国，她的实验室的镭几乎不超过一克。梅洛尼惊问她只有一克吗，她纠正说，那不是她的，而是属于她的实验室。梅洛尼那一周得知，一克镭市价十万美元。她的实验室虽然几乎是新楼，设备并不够用，那里的镭当时只用于为医院提取射气治疗癌症。梅洛尼原想几周后到纽约时，找十位女士各出一万美元买下一克，免去公开募捐的声势，结果只找到一两位。后来是十万名妇女和一批男士下决心要把钱募齐，不到一年基金就募成了。据居里夫人自己的记述，一个由几位知名女士和杰出科学家组成的委员会收到一些重要捐赠，并发起公众认捐，许多妇女组织、尤其是大学和俱乐部纷纷响应，不少捐款来自受益于镭疗法的人。就这样，集成了超过十万美元的居里夫人镭基金。

Meloney wrote the introduction to the book and later launched the subscription in New York. When she met Curie, Curie said that America had about fifty grammes of radium: four of these in Baltimore, six in Denver, seven in New York, and on she went, naming the location of every grain. And in France? "My laboratory," she said, "has hardly more than a gramme." Meloney, astonished, exclaimed that she had only a gramme. "I? Oh, I have none," Curie corrected. "It belongs to my laboratory." That week Meloney learned that the market price of a gramme of radium was one hundred thousand dollars. She also learned that Curie's laboratory, although practically a new building, was without sufficient equipment, and that the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use in cancer treatment. When she arrived in New York a few weeks afterwards, Meloney had hoped to find ten women to subscribe ten thousand dollars each and buy a gramme without the publicity of a general campaign. She found one or two. There were not ten women to buy that gramme of radium, but there were a hundred thousand women and a group of men determined that the money must be raised, and in less than a year the fund had been raised. In Curie's own account, a committee including several prominent women and distinguished scientific men received some important gifts and made an appeal for a public subscription. A great number of women's organizations, especially colleges and clubs, responded, and in many cases gifts came from persons who had experienced the benefit of radiumtherapy. In this way the "Marie Curie Radium Fund" of more than one hundred thousand dollars was collected.

据梅洛尼记述，仪式前一夜又出了岔子：文件要把这一克镭放在居里夫人个人名下。她读完说不行。这一克镭代表很多钱，可它更代表美国的妇女，不是给她的，是给科学的。她身体不好，随时可能死；女儿伊夫尚未成年，一旦她去世，镭就会进她的遗产，由两个女儿分掉。她要求当晚就把文件办好，因为第二天就要接收镭。于是那个闷热的五月夜晚，虽然已经很晚，他们还是请到律师，照她自拟的草稿写好文件。她在动身去华盛顿前签了字：她死后，这一克镭归巴黎的镭研究所，供居里实验室专用。第二天在白宫，哈定总统交给她的是一把小金钥匙。

As Meloney tells it, on the eve of the ceremony there was one more snag: the papers were to put this gramme of radium in Curie's own name. She read them and said it must not be left that way. The gramme represented a great deal of money, but more than that it represented the women of the country: it was not for her, it was for science. She was not well and might die any day. Her daughter Eve was not of legal age, and if she died the radium would go into her estate and be divided between her daughters. That was not its purpose; it had to be consecrated for all time to the use of science. The paper had to be fixed that night, because the next day she received the radium, and, she said, as Meloney reports it, "I might die tomorrow. Too much is at stake." So, late as it was on that hot May evening, a lawyer was secured and prepared the paper from a draft Curie herself had written. She signed it before starting for Washington: in the event of her death the gramme of radium went to the Institut du Radium in Paris, for the exclusive use of the Laboratoire Curie. The next day at the White House, what she received from President Harding was the small golden key.
作者推断，这套选择的代价不是一次性的损失，而是一条链。方法公开后，工业自由发展，医生和科学家很快拿到了产品；同时矿物涨价，镭价居高不下。她的实验室设备不足，那里的镭当时只用于为医院提取射气；她亲手制得的一克多镭，全都给了实验室。一种解释是，他们用自己后来的研究条件，替整个行业垫了启动成本。

The author's reading is that the cost of these choices was not a single loss but a chain. The method went public; the industry developed freely; physicians and scientists got their products quickly. At the same time the minerals got dearer and the price of radium stayed high. Her laboratory was without sufficient equipment, and the radium held there was used at that time only for extracting emanations for hospital use; the gramme and more that Marie Curie prepared with her own hands had gone entirely to the laboratory. One way to put it: they paid the start-up costs of a whole industry out of their own research conditions.
她在自传笔记里给出了自己的说法（这是她的主张，不是可核对的事实）。人类需要实干者，他们为自身利益好好做事，同时不忘公共利益；人类也需要做梦者，他们一门心思追随目标，顾不上自己的物质好处。也许有人会说，这些理想主义者既然不想要财富，也就不配得到财富。但她认为，组织良好的社会应当给这样的工作者以高效工作的条件，让他们的生活没有物质之忧，可以专心服务科学研究。

She gave her own account of it in the autobiographical notes, and it is her position, not a fact that can be checked: humanity needs practical men who make the best of their work for the sake of their own interests without forgetting the general interest, but it also needs dreamers, for whom the unselfish following of a purpose is so imperative that it becomes impossible for them to devote much attention to their own material benefit. No doubt it could be said that these idealists do not deserve riches, since they do not have the desire for them. A society well organized, she thought, ought to assure to these workers the means for efficient labor, in a life from which material care is excluded, so that the life may be freely devoted to the service of scientific research.
作者提出另一种做法（书中没有写他们讨论过任何替代方案）：分用途授权，研究与教学免费，商业开发收费；或者只对产品收费，把方法留在公共领域。这条路或许能留下一点收入，代价是谈判、监督，以及与工业界的长期纠缠。朋友们主张的则是保留权利、用收益建研究所。差别不在谁更高尚，而在谁承担风险。

The author's alternative, and the book records no such discussion: license by use, free for research and teaching and charged for commercial exploitation, or else charge for the product and leave the method in the public domain. Some income might have been kept that way, at the price of negotiation, oversight, and a long entanglement with industry. What the friends urged was retaining the rights and building the institute out of the proceeds. The difference is not who is nobler; it is who carries the risk.
今天常见的一幕：一位医院检验科的技师，把自己改良多年的样本处理流程写成公开文档，几家同行医院都用上了。可她科室的设备还是老几样，添置经费排在队尾。她要判断的不是自己够不够高尚，而是方法公开之后，谁来付下一轮改进的账。

A familiar scene today: a hospital laboratory technician writes up the sample-processing method she has refined over many years as an open document, and several peer hospitals start using it. Her own department is still running the same old equipment, and the request for new purchases sits at the end of the queue. What she has to judge is not whether she is noble enough, but who pays for the next round of improvements once the method is public.
